transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-04
Time: 15:00 PST (scheduled 60m)
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Lena Martin (Redwood AE), Dmitri Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (NorthGate Procurement), Raj Patel (NorthGate Security), Eve Thompson (NorthGate Legal), Tom Alvarez (Cloud Ops)

Summary:
Quick sync to map PO intake and how the MSA/DPA/SLA flow should look, clarify data residency requirements for EU patient data, and get timelines for pricing approvals. Customer needs PO process doc + security artifacts. SE to plan POC for perf validation.

Topics:
- Purchase order and billing flow (PO numbers, invoicing entity, net terms)
- MSA & DPA redlines and timing for legal review
- SLA guarantees and escalation path for production incidents
- Data residency (EU region hosting vs pseudonymization) and encryption/K M S questions
- POC/benchmarks and procurement gating criteria

Action items (also captured above): see list.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: ok everyone thanks for joining, uh, we'll try to keep to the hour, this is the PO intake and SLA escalation sync, so high level we'll cover the contract path and any redlines, and then Dmitri can speak to the POC needs.
[00:15] Maya: thanks Lena, for context procurement timeline is about 3 to 6 weeks depending on legal redlines and finance sign-off. we need a PO template and a clear invoice flow, uh net30 is preferred but we may request net45 for some vendors.
[00:30] Lena: understood, we'll include both net30 and net45 options in the pricing sheet. we'll also note who needs to receive the invoice — is that finance@northgate.org?
[00:42] Maya: that's right. also need to confirm the billing entity name is "NorthGate Health Systems, Inc." and the tax id will be provided once PO is ready.
[00:58] Raj: hi all, from security side a couple of redlines matter: SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certificates, K M S integration for key management, and audit logs retention for minimum 7 years for our regulatory audits. also need clarity on where data at rest will be — specifically EU PHI needs to stay in eu-west-1 or a dedicated on-prem cluster.
[01:15] Dmitri: okay, for K M S we support customer-managed K M S (okta? I mean KMS via cloud providers) and we can run private deployments inside a VPC or on-prem where required. there is a small perf delta for private but we can quantify that in the POC.
[01:33] Eve: from legal: we will look for DPA amendments about processor-subprocessor chains, breach notification timing (72 hours ideally), and we may request a narrow data residency clause that prohibits cross-border replication without consent. also indemnities and liability caps need to be clarified in the MSA.
[01:50] Lena: yep we can provide standard MSA + DPA and we'll flag any clauses that are often negotiated. quick question for financing though: do you require Redwood to accept purchase orders as the primary source of obligation, or do you need a signed MSA before PO is issued?
[02:05] Maya: usually our process is PO first if the terms are standard; if there are material redlines we need a signed MSA. so the risk is the redline path may flip the timeline to the longer side.
[02:18] Lena: got it, so we'll try to keep the DPA/MSA conservative and identify must-haves vs negotiables in the redline doc. we'll label any true blockers so you can fast-track through procurement.
[02:33] Tom: one operational ask — we need a clear escalation path in the SLA for production incidents; that includes a P1 contact list, expected response times, and runbooks or RCA windows. also we need to know if you offer a SOC 2 + syslogs push to our SIEM.
[02:50] Dmitri: SLA-wise our standard is 99.9% for hosted, with SLOs for median latency and tail latency, and a 15-minute P1 initial response for enterprise tier; we can commit to shorter response windows under a dedicated contract. regarding syslogs we have an integration pattern to push audit logs via S3 or a direct syslog sink; we also support pushing to common SIEMs through an ingestion connector.
[03:15] Raj: you mentioned 15 minutes for enterprise, can that be escalated to 5 minutes if we buy the higher SLA? we have to evaluate that against our on-call rotation.
[03:26] Lena: yes for Dedicated customers we generally have a faster initial response SLA and a named escalation path, we can put an explicit 5 minute P1 ack if that's required with the right enterprise contract.
[03:40] Maya: and for approval — pricing committees want to see TCO comparisons and the invoice cadence. can you provide an example invoice and an estimated monthly burn for our expected volume?
[03:52] Lena: sure, we'll send a pricing sheet with sample invoice lines (per-token, embeddings, reserved capacity), and we'll include a modeled estimate for the 1M tokens/day scenario you mentioned earlier.
[04:05] Dmitri: on the POC: typical setup is 1-2 days of data prep, then a 3-5 day perf run where we feed representative queries to measure throughput and tail latency. we'll need a small test dataset — anonymized — and network access to run the tests.
[04:25] Raj: for PHI we can't use real patient data; we will create a synthetic set that mirrors the size and cardinality. do you have guidance on scrubbing or pseudonymization?
[04:36] Dmitri: yes, we can share a sanitization checklist. usually we recommend pseudonymizing IDs and removing direct identifiers, we can accept hashed tokens for alignment. we'll add that to the POC plan.
[04:50] Eve: one point on DPA — we may need a clause enforcing that Redwood's subprocessors are named or at least that you'll provide a subprocessor list 30 days in advance. also deletion and return of data upon contract termination is key.
[05:05] Lena: absolutely, our DPA template includes subprocessor notification and a standard data deletion clause; if you'd like we can add explicit 30-day notice language.
[05:18] Maya: also a small procurement wrinkle — our finance team requires the vendor to accept purchase orders with a reference to the MSA; they prefer a clause that a valid PO plus the MSA equals the contract. will Redwood accept that?
[05:32] Lena: we can accept that wording, generally Redwood accepts POs that reference the MSA. we'll add an example PO acceptance clause to the docs we send.
[05:45] Tom: another ops ask — do you support regional pinning so traffic and KV cache stay in eu-west-1? otherwise cross-region replication could be a compliance problem for us.
[05:58] Dmitri: yes, we support region pinning and can restrict replica placement; for hosted accounts we can ensure instances in eu-west-1 only. if you need guaranteed single-tenant isolation we can propose a private deployment. note: private will require networking and slightly different onboarding steps.
[06:15] Raj: do you have encryption at rest with customer-managed keys? we need to show the K M S integration diagram to our auditors.
[06:25] Dmitri: yes, we support CMK with the major cloud K M S providers; we will provide an architecture diagram and also HSM details if needed.
[06:38] Eve: on liability caps — we typically push for a higher cap for data breaches, and we will seek carveouts for willful misconduct. are you open to discussion?
[06:49] Lena: open to discussion; our default MSA has a liability cap tied to annualized fees, but we can look at tailoring that for regulated workloads. we'll flag that as a legal discussion item.
[07:02] Maya: can you also provide a timeline expectation for the legal review? from our side, if we get redlines by Monday, we can turn around within 7-10 business days depending on wording.
[07:16] Lena: we will aim to send redlines and a marked MSA by 2026-12-06. Eve, can you confirm availability for the 12-08 legal call?
[07:27] Eve: yes 12-08 at 10am ET works for me for a 30-45 minute call.
[07:34] Tom: final ops note — do you offer an extended retention for audit logs beyond 7 years? our policy requires 10 for certain data classes.
[07:44] Dmitri: we can negotiate retention-based add ons; standard is 7 years but extended retention is possible, it'll affect storage pricing.
[07:58] Lena: ok, quick recap of next steps: Redwood to send MSA+DPA+security pack+pricing+PO template by 12-06; Dmitri to produce POC plan by 12-09; customer to confirm PO timeline and provide list of must-have DPA clauses by 12-07.
[08:18] Maya: sounds good. one more question — do you have a standard ordering flow for marketplace purchases vs direct POs? sometimes our procurement prefers marketplace for ease of payment.
[08:31] Lena: we are in a couple marketplaces; for enterprise customers we usually do direct PO for billing and contractual control, but we can discuss if marketplace is acceptable — one tradeoff is less flexible SSO/K M S integration in some marketplaces.
[08:50] Raj: any thoughts on whether this can fit into our Fed ramp path? we are early in our FedRAMP assessment and wondered if Redwood has any certifications or a Fed ramp roadmap.
[09:03] Dmitri: we don't yet have Fed ramp certification, short of that our security pack includes SOC 2 Type II, the controls matrix, and we can provide artifacts to help with ATO documentation. we do offer private deployments that are easier to include in FedRAMP plans.
[09:20] Eve: ok, if we need FedRAMP we may simply do a private deployment and have Redwood as a managed service inside our boundary. but that's a larger conversation after initial procurement.
[09:32] Lena: understood. any final clarifying questions?
[09:38] Maya: none from procurement, just need the docs.
[09:41] Raj: please include the K M S diagram and subprocessor list.
[09:45] Lena: will do. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with attachments and calendar invites for the legal and POC calls.
[09:55] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (K M S spaced, Fed ramp), speaker overlap at times, and some technical terms simplified by the AI transcription.
